en: The *Sūtra on the Divine Incantations Spoken by the Illusionist Bhadra*, also known as the *Sūtra on the Divine Incantations Spoken by the Mystical Master Bhadra*, translated by the Tripitaka Master Zhu Tanwulan of the Western Regions during the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was dwelling in the Bamboo Grove of the Parrot [Monastery] in the kingdom of Rājagṛha.
Among the trees.
At that time, there was a certain bhikṣu who was traveling from Rājagṛha toward the Bamboo Grove.
While traveling on the middle path, he was bitten by a venomous snake,
further harassed by malevolent spirits,
and additionally plundered by bandits.
When the Buddha saw this, he immediately went to where that bhikṣu was.
The illusionist Bhadra followed along with the Buddha.
The illusionist Bhadra then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I possess a technique that is most profound and wondrous;
I now wish to perform a mantra.
The Buddha said, "Stop, stop, Bhadra!"
"Ensure that what you have spoken does not cause harm.
Bhadrapāla addressed the Buddha, saying,
"In future ages..."
When states attack one another, thieves plunder one another;
those who hate one another further plunder one another;
even ghosts and spirits plunder one another.
Poisons further harm one another.
Suppose there is a bhikṣu sitting beneath a tree in the mountains,
wearing his five-layered rag-robe, or perhaps sitting in the open air.
May the fourfold assembly of disciples be free from those who can cause harm;
may they all be secure and free from illness and pain.

*Svāhā śarīṇi uccharī śūri śūri vartisaṃtiprāptani apaye daryu acchijja yahe vartilūḍha saṃśrite svāhā saṃtiprāptani maṇḍalāhūna vijahūna.* By this incantation, may verbal disputes be severed, may all sorceries be severed, and may all illnesses and pains be severed.
All these yakṣas perform this rite: the Sūma-guhyaka, the Mahāyakṣa Ghoṣananda, the Yakṣa Brahmakumāra, the Mahāyakṣa Indrāgnikumāra, and the Mahāyakṣa Aṅgiras.
These yakṣas are the most honored among the spirits and deities.
My name is Indu; I cause those who seek various marks, those who are afflicted by the diseases of desire, and those who harm others [to attain peace].
I shall cause them all to be unaware of my location;
I will obstruct and confuse their vision so that they cannot see me,
ensuring that no person whatsoever can gain any advantage over me.
At that time, he called out: "Come!
Mahāpālaka, the spirit, come! Mahāpālaka, come!
Daulika, Mahādaulika, come!"
Indrahasta and Mahāindrahasta came; Brahmahasta and Mahābrahmahasta came;
Indrahasta and Mahāindrahasta came.
Bodhadūta mahābodhadūta come!
Yakṣadūta mahāyakṣadūta come! Ātattodula mahāātattodula come!
Śūla, Goṣa, Durlabha, Mahāśūla, Goṣa, Durlabha. As for me,
named Indu, whenever various enemies seek out an opportunity to harm me,
I rescue them all and shield them from harm.
Causing the two not to see each other,
bound by ropes and cords;
the destruction of that which binds.
Bound by malice, bound by a mind intoxicated by desire,
and bound by a distracted mind.
"Simply by taking refuge in the Buddha, all shall attain liberation.
When taking refuge in the Buddha, one says 'Namo Buddha,' rises to perform a prostration, and departs.
— *The Sūtra of the Illusionist Bhadra’s Divine Spells* (Huan shi batuo shenzhou jing)
